question.text: An exporter buys 200 lots of USDINR 84.00 put at Rs. 0.25 to hedge. At expiry, USDINR is 85.50. What does the exporter do and what is the effective rate?

answer.text: Let put expire worthless, sell at spot 85.50. Effective rate = Rs. 85.25 (85.50 - 0.25 premium)
Exercise put, sell at 84.00. Effective rate = Rs. 83.75
Let put expire, effective rate = Rs. 85.50
Exercise put at 84.00. Effective rate = Rs. 84.00

explanation.text: The Logic: At expiry USDINR = 85.50, the 84.00 protective put is out-of-the-money for the exporter, so it expires worthless. The exporter sells USD at the higher spot of 85.50 and bears only the premium already paid. Effective rate = 85.50 - 0.25 = Rs. 85.25 per USD. Loss on the option is limited to the premium. The Trap: Option B exercises an OTM put and reports the floor (Strike - Premium = 83.75), which is irrational at this spot. Option C ignores the premium that was paid up-front. Option D exercises at the strike and ignores both the premium and the favourable spot. Note: Distributor-specific and cross-exam framing removed; explanation kept to neutral protective-put wording (let OTM put lapse, net premium against higher spot).
